Verse 1 — Honest measures

People may treat false weights and measures as a small offense, especially when the practice is widespread, but God regards such dishonesty as detestable.

Verse 2 — The safety of humility

The humble enjoy greater security, peace and ease of mind than the proud. Wisdom belongs with humility.

Verse 3 — Integrity guides life

An honest person's principles are settled, so the right path is clear.

Verse 4 — Money cannot save us from death

Wealth offers no help when the day of death arrives.

Verses 5 and 6 — Sin destroys its own followers

Wicked ways are dangerous. Sin eventually becomes its own punishment.

Verse 7 — What death removes

When a godly person dies, all fears vanish. When an ungodly person dies, all false hopes vanish.

Verse 8 — Providence preserves the upright

The righteous are often wonderfully kept from danger, while the wicked fall into the trouble they escaped.

Verse 9 — The dangers of hypocritical speech

Hypocrites mislead others into wrongdoing by using clever objections to God's word.

Verses 10 and 11 — A community relieved of wickedness

A nation prospers when wicked people lose their power to injure it.

Verse 12 — Judge character, not success

A person of understanding does not judge someone else's worth merely by outward prosperity.

Verse 13 — Keep confidences faithfully

A trustworthy person keeps confidential matters private, unless God's honor or the genuine good of society requires disclosure.

Verse 14 — The value of counsel

Consulting others often brings important advantages. We should not assume our judgment needs no advice.

Verse 15 — Consider the cost of guaranteeing debts

Do not endanger your family's welfare, your peace of mind or your ability to pay rightful debts by undertaking obligations you cannot meet. But remember the extraordinary grace of Jesus Christ, who became Surety for his enemies.

Verse 16 — The honor of a wise woman

A godly, prudent woman preserves respect and esteem as firmly as strong people protect their wealth.

Verse 17 — Cruelty harms the cruel

A cruel, ill-tempered person causes suffering to those who ought to be treated as his own flesh, and punishes himself through that cruelty.

Verse 18 — Doing good has a sure reward

Those who make doing good their work have a reward as certain as God's eternal truth.

Verse 19 — Holiness is happiness

True holiness brings true happiness. The more fiercely someone pursues sin, the faster destruction approaches.

Verse 20 — God hates double dealing

Nothing is more offensive to God than hypocrisy and deceit. He delights in people whose intentions and conduct are sincere.

Verse 21 — A crowd cannot protect sinners

Joining together with others to commit sin does not make anyone safe from judgment.

Verse 22 — Beauty without discretion

Physical beauty is misused when separated from modesty and sound judgment. The same applies to other bodily advantages.

Verse 23 — Evil desires recoil upon their owner

Wicked people desire harm for others, but their schemes return upon themselves.

Verse 24 — Misers can lose what they withhold

People may become poor by refusing to pay just debts, help the poor or meet necessary expenses. Even careful hoarding can come to nothing whenever God so appoints.

Verse 25 — Generosity and God's provision

In spiritual and earthly matters, God commonly treats his people according to the measure of generosity they show their neighbors.

Verse 26 — Do not hoard God's gifts

We must not store up the blessings of God's bounty only to advance our own interests.

Verse 27 — Seek good, not harm

Seeking harm is contrasted with seeking good. Those who refuse to do good may be doing harm even to themselves.

Verse 28 — The living Vine

A believer is a branch of the living Vine, Christ. Those rooted only in worldly wealth will wither, but people grafted into Christ will bear fruit.

Verse 29 — Troubling your household

Someone who brings suffering upon self and family through wickedness or carelessness will lose the ability to hold and enjoy possessions—just as no one can grasp the wind or be satisfied by it.

Verse 30 — Righteousness nourishes others

The righteous are like trees of life. The influence of their lives nourishes and supports spiritual life in many others.

Verse 31 — Seek the blessings Christ purchased

Even righteous people meet severe correction when they sin on earth. How much more will the wicked receive their deserved judgment! Seek the blessings our Surety purchased through his suffering and death, imitate his example and keep his commands.

modern_osis:
Verse 1 — Love instruction

People who possess God's grace welcome instruction and correction. Those who suppress conviction behave like unreasoning animals.

Verse 2 — Disguised evil remains evil

Someone who conceals selfish and corrupt plans under the outward appearance of religion or friendship will be condemned.

Verse 3 — An enduring foundation

People may rise through dishonest methods, but they cannot become secure through them. Those who are rooted in Christ by faith are firmly established.

Verse 4 — A wife who brings honor

A godly and prudent wife who manages her household well, performs her duties conscientiously and patiently endures hardship brings honor and comfort to her husband. A wife who does the opposite causes him distress and drains his strength.

Verse 5 — God knows our thoughts

Thoughts are not beyond moral accountability. God knows them, and they are therefore subject to his commands. Scheming and deceit bring shame.

Verse 6 — Words can wound or help

Wicked people use their words to injure neighbors. Yet even one good word can sometimes accomplish a valuable work.

Verse 7 — The households of the righteous

God's blessing often continues within the families of godly people even when the wicked are brought down.

Verse 8 — Wisdom in suffering disgrace

The apostles displayed wisdom by rejoicing to suffer dishonor for Christ's name.

Verse 9 — Humble sufficiency

Someone who works for daily bread without servants is happier than a person boasting of noble ancestry or fine clothing while lacking life's necessities.

Verse 10 — Kindness to animals

A godly person does not impose unnecessary pain even on an animal. Wicked people may describe as merciful treatment that they themselves could not bear for a single day.

Verse 11 — Attend to honest work

It is wise to work diligently at an honest occupation. Neglecting ordinary responsibilities is folly; God's grace teaches us to despise nothing except sin.

Verse 12 — Do not envy unlawful gains

When wicked people see others prospering through sin, they may wish to imitate them. But God's grace rooted in the righteous heart produces different desires and aims.

Verse 13 — The costly misuse of speech

Many people have paid dearly, even during this life, for sins committed with their lips.

Verse 14 — Speech that serves others

People who rightly use their words to instruct and comfort others enjoy acceptance through Jesus Christ and the conscience's encouragement that they have, in some measure, fulfilled their purpose.

Verse 15 — The fool's own standard

In Scripture the fool is a wicked person who rejects wisdom from above. The rule of life becomes whatever is right in that person's own eyes.

Verse 16 — Restrain anger

A fool becomes angry quickly and displays it recklessly, thereby inviting trouble. We treat ourselves kindly when we overlook insults rather than making the worst of them.

Verse 17 — Be ruled by truth

Everyone should regard lying with abhorrence and be guided by honest speech.

Verse 18 — A healing tongue

Whispered accusations and unfounded suspicions cut like swords, separating even close friends. But the speech of wise people brings healing.

Verse 19 — Truth endures

Truth remains firm and valid even when people dislike hearing it.

Verse 20 — Peace brings joy

Deceit and lies bring terror and confusion. Those who seek others' peace and happiness find joy in their own hearts.

Verse 21 — The security of the righteous

God has promised protection to those who are genuinely righteous. But people who delight in causing harm will experience plenty of harm themselves.

Verse 22 — Truthful words and conduct

Make honesty a matter of conscience in actions as well as words.

Verse 23 — Folly announces itself

Foolish people publicly expose the emptiness and folly of their own thinking.

Verse 24 — Diligence is honorable

People who avoid honest work and try to survive through tricks and dishonesty reduce themselves to a miserable condition.

Verse 25 — Encouragement in anxiety

Worry, fear and sorrow weaken people's strength for duty and courage in suffering. A good word from God, received through faith, restores joy to the heart.

Verse 26 — Real riches in the Spirit

Righteous people possess abundance even when they lack worldly wealth: the Spirit's graces and comforts are true riches. Wicked people falsely assure themselves their chosen way is harmless.

Verse 27 — Use opportunities well

Lazy people waste the advantages Providence has given and receive no comfort from them. The diligent person's possessions, even if modest, bless that person and the family and are received gratefully as God's answer to prayer.

Verse 28 — Life on the path

True religion leads along a straight and clearly marked way of righteousness. Life is found not only at the end of the path but along it, through genuine spiritual comfort.

Chapter 12
Verse 1
Those who have grace, will delight in the instructions given them. Those that stifle their convictions, are like brutes.

modern_osis:
Verse 1 — Respect faithful correction

Children who honor their parents give reason for hope. Little hope remains for those who refuse to listen to people who faithfully correct them.

Verse 2 — Accountability for speech

By our words we will be justified or condemned (Matthew 12:37).

Verse 3 — Guard the tongue

Thinking before we speak, and refusing to utter evil thoughts, protects the soul from much guilt and grief. Many have ruined themselves through an uncontrolled tongue.

Verse 4 — Desire without diligence

Lazy people desire what diligent people gain but refuse the effort needed to obtain it. Their desires remain unsatisfied. This is especially true in spiritual life.

Verse 5 — Sin makes us repulsive

Where sin rules, a person becomes detestable. A conscience awakened to sin would lead to self-abhorrence and repentance in dust and ashes.

Verse 6 — A sincere desire to do right

The honest determination to do what is right guards a person from disastrous mistakes more effectively than a thousand elaborate distinctions.

Verse 7 — Poverty and wealth can be appearances

Some people are poor but spend and trade as though rich; this is sinful and leads toward shame. Others are wealthy but pretend to be poor, showing ingratitude to God and injustice and lack of charity toward others. Many hypocrites lack grace but refuse to see their poverty. Many timid Christians possess great spiritual riches yet believe themselves poor; their doubt, complaint and sorrow make them unnecessarily miserable.

Verse 8 — Riches invite dangers

Great wealth can expose its owner to threats and violence from which the poor are often free.

Verse 9 — Light that endures

A righteous person's light resembles the sun: clouds or an eclipse may obscure it, but it continues to shine. The Spirit is their light and gives full joy. The wicked person's light is like a lamp lit by human hands, easily extinguished.

Verse 10 — Pride feeds quarrels

Disputes between people, families, churches and nations begin and continue through pride. Without pride, disagreements would often be prevented or quickly settled.

Verse 11 — Dishonest wealth wastes away

Wealth obtained through fraud or sin carries a hidden curse and soon disappears.

Verse 12 — Hope delayed and fulfilled

Long delays in receiving something eagerly expected cause pain; receiving it brings delight. Henry says spiritual blessings are chiefly in view here.

Verse 13 — Reverence for God's word

Those who fear God and honor his word escape destruction and receive the reward of reverent obedience.

Verse 14 — Wisdom is a fountain

The principles that guide a wise person's life become a fountain of life and happiness.

Verse 15 — Sin is harsh slavery

The sinner's path harms other people and the sinner too. Serving sin is slavery, and the road toward hell is strewn with the thorns and thistles of the curse.

Verse 16 — Do not speak beyond knowledge

It is foolish to speak confidently on subjects we know nothing about or to undertake work we are wholly unqualified to perform.

Verse 17 — Faithful messengers bring healing

Those who are unfaithful to Christ and other people's souls bring and suffer harm. Faithful messengers find that sound words heal both themselves and those who hear them.

Verse 18 — Despising instruction leads down

Those who refuse to be taught will eventually be humbled.

Verse 19 — The false pleasure of sin

Human beings long intensely for happiness. But people unwilling to abandon their sins should not expect any sweetness that can truly satisfy their souls.

Verse 20 — Choose companions wisely

Bad company brings multitudes to ruin. Those who make themselves wicked will be destroyed.

Verse 21 — God's justice overtakes sinners

When God pursues sinners in judgment, he will overtake them. He will also reward the righteous.

Verse 22 — The best provision for children

A servant of God who does not live in anxiety over becoming wealthy is actually following the best way to provide for children.

Verse 23 — Industry and discernment

Poor people who work hard may prosper modestly, while those with great resources often become poor through foolish management.

Verse 24 — Loving discipline

Parents who indulgently allow sinful habits to grow strong act as though they hated their children. Such habits bring sorrow now and may bring misery hereafter.

Verse 25 — What truly satisfies

Wicked people find that even their bodily appetites continually demand more. The righteous feed their souls on God's word and appointed ordinances, finding satisfaction in gospel promises and Jesus Christ, the Bread of Life.

modern_osis:
Verse 1 — A household built or destroyed

A woman who has no fear of God and is willful, wasteful and given to ease can ruin her own household as surely as if she pulled down its walls.

Verse 2 — Reverence or contempt

Here grace and sin show their true character. Whoever despises God's commands and promises also despises God's power and mercy.

Verse 3 — Uproot pride

Pride grows from bitterness rooted in the heart. We must pull out the root, not merely cut off one visible branch. Wise and prudent words can help people escape difficulties.

Verse 4 — Useful work involves some inconvenience

No real advantage is obtained without some difficulty or inconvenience—often something small that nevertheless frightens lazy people.

Verse 5 — Witness truthfully

A conscientious witness will never knowingly describe events differently from what he or she actually knows.

Verse 6 — Humility receives wisdom

A scoffer treats God's truth with contempt. Someone conscious of ignorance and unworthiness approaches Scripture humbly.

Verse 7 — Recognize unholy conversation

A person's speech can reveal wickedness when no evidence of reverence for God can be found in it.

Verse 8 — Know the road and its destination

We are travelers. Our concern is not to stare at extraordinary sights, but to learn the rules for our journey and the destination toward which we walk. The wicked person deceives himself and continues in error.

Verse 9 — Do not mock sin or atonement

Careless people treat sin as something trivial, rather than something to grieve over. Fools mock the sin offering, and those who treat sin lightly also treat Christ lightly.

Verse 10 — Hidden pain and hidden peace

We do not know what guilt or consuming passions torment an apparently prosperous sinner. Nor does the world understand a sincere Christian's inward peace, even amid poverty and sickness.

Verse 11 — What upholds a household

Sin has ruined many important families, while righteousness often strengthens and raises households of humble standing.

Verse 12 — Self-deception leads to destruction

Careless, worldly and sensual paths can seem right to those traveling them. Those who deceive themselves may destroy themselves. The joy promised by fleshly pleasure is vain.

Verse 14 — The dread of returning to sin

Of all sinners, people who have knowingly turned away from their former faith can experience especially terrible fear when reflecting upon their course.

Verse 15 — Do not believe everything

Readiness to believe anyone's claims can be deeply harmful; Henry recalls how the world first fell through misplaced trust. Spiritually wise people rely on the Savior alone for acceptance and guard themselves through God's word.

Verse 16 — Holy fear protects

Reverent fear of God guards us against everything unholy.

Verse 17 — Anger and revenge

Someone who loses their temper quickly deserves both rebuke and pity. Deliberate revengefulness is still more hateful.

Verse 18 — Wisdom brings honor

Sin brings shame upon sinners; wisdom brings honor to the wise.

Verse 19 — Goodness recognized even by enemies

Even wicked people sometimes have to acknowledge the excellence of God's faithful servants.

Verse 20 — Friendship beyond self-interest

Worldly friendship often depends on personal advantage. How good it is to have God as our Friend: he will never abandon us.

Verse 21 — Do not despise poverty

Looking down on someone because of occupation, clothing or outward appearance is sinful.

Verse 22 — Plan to do good

Those who not only do good but actively devise ways of doing good wisely pursue their own best interests.

Verse 23 — Real work versus empty talk

Both intellectual and manual labor can produce good results. But religion consisting only of loud words without action will achieve nothing.

Verse 24 — Use wealth for good

The possessions of wise and godly people should enlarge their opportunities to be useful to others.

Verse 25 — Courageous truthful testimony

An upright witness will risk even the displeasure of powerful people rather than conceal the truth.

Verses 26 and 27 — Reverent confidence and the fountain of life

Those who fear the Lord so as to obey and serve him have a solid basis for confidence and will be kept in his care. Seek this fountain of life and escape death's traps.

Verse 28 — Seek the growth of Christ's kingdom

Everyone who desires the good of Christ's kingdom should do what they can to bring more people into his church.

Verse 29 — Patience resembles Christ

A gentle and patient person is learning from Christ, who is Wisdom. Uncontrolled passion reveals folly.

Verse 30 — A peaceful heart helps health

Integrity, contentment and kindness contribute toward the well-being of the body.

Verse 1 — Gentle words calm anger

A just cause is better defended with gentleness than with a hot temper. Nothing provokes anger more quickly than harsh words.

Verse 2 — Share knowledge for others' benefit

Those who possess knowledge ought to use it wisely for the good of other people.

Verse 3 — Nothing is hidden from God

God sees every secret sin, secret act of service and secret sorrow. His knowledge comforts the faithful and warns the ungodly.

Verse 4 — The healing power of speech

Kind and truthful speech brings healing to wounded consciences by comfort, convinces spiritually sick souls of their need, and reconciles people who have quarreled.

Verse 5 — Do not let others walk toward ruin

When people reject instruction, we should continue to correct them faithfully rather than allow them to proceed undisturbed toward destruction.

Verse 6 — Worldly wealth can multiply fears

The riches of those devoted to the world may increase their suspicion, stir their passions and make the fear of death still more distressing.

Verse 7 — Spread good knowledge

We use knowledge well when we share it with others. Foolish people's hearts have little that is good to offer.

Verses 8 and 9 — Christ's atonement and sincere obedience

The wicked try to place other things in the place of Christ's atonement or of holy obedience. The grace to pray rightly is God's gift and the Spirit's work, which is pleasing to him.

Verse 10 — Do not reject reproof

People who hate correction and refuse to part with their sins will perish in them.

Verse 11 — Even human thoughts are open

Nothing can be hidden from God—not even the deepest thoughts of the heart.

Verse 12 — The scorner avoids self-examination

Someone who mocks holiness cannot endure seriously examining the condition of the heart.

Verse 13 — The misery of a gloomy spirit

A continually ungrateful, impatient and darkened spirit—often nourished by pride and excessive attachment to worldly things—makes life difficult for oneself and others.

Verse 14 — Continue growing in wisdom

Wise people seek further wisdom, growing in grace and knowledge of Christ. Worldly minds rest content while flattering themselves.

Verse 15 — Comfort the suffering and rejoice reverently

People weighed down by suffering and sorrow deserve pity, prayer and comfort. Others serve God joyfully and find that joy strengthens obedience, yet they should still rejoice with reverence.

Verses 16 and 17 — Enough with the Lord

God's people may possess enough while worldly observers think they have almost nothing. The Lord's presence is better than the worries, temptations and troubles that accompany ungodly wealth.

Verse 18 — Be slow to anger

Patient people not only avoid starting quarrels, but can also calm conflicts once they begin.

Verse 19 — Laziness invents obstacles

Those unwilling to work imagine excessive hardship or danger in their duties. Many also remain uncertain about their spiritual condition because they keep neglecting some known duty.

Verse 20 — Honor aging parents

Contempt for an elderly father or mother reveals a person's own foolishness.

Verse 21 — Wisdom shapes the whole life

Truly wise people seek to keep thoughts, words and actions orderly, sincere and holy.

Verse 22 — Think before acting

People unwilling to take time and effort to consult and deliberate are unlikely to accomplish their plans.

Verse 23 — Speak appropriately

Wisdom is needed to fit our words to the occasion.

Verse 24 — Set the heart on heaven

A godly person sets affections upon the things above, and life's path leads toward them.

Verse 25 — God opposes pride and supports the afflicted

Pride has destroyed multitudes, but God upholds those who are suffering.

Verse 26 — God knows sinful thoughts

Wicked thoughts offend the Lord, who knows what is within the heart.

Verse 27 — Greed troubles the family

Covetous people deprive their own households of peace and enjoyment. Greed often entices them into reckless projects that end in ruin.

Verse 28 — Wisdom governs speech

A godly person's wise control over the tongue is evidence of genuine wisdom.

Verse 29 — Rebellion creates distance

God withdraws his favor from people who openly defy him.

Verse 30 — The joyful news of salvation

How wonderful it is for a humbled soul to hear the good news of salvation through the Lord Jesus Christ!

Verse 31 — A kind rebuke is a gift

Faithful and friendly correction supports spiritual life and leads toward eternal life.

Verse 32 — Do not sacrifice the soul for the body

Sinners undervalue their own souls and therefore prefer bodily pleasure even when it harms the soul.

Verse 33 — Reverence, Scripture and grace

The fear of God moves us to search the Scriptures reverently and follow the Holy Spirit's leading. As we humbly depend on God's grace, we are exalted through Christ's righteousness.

Verse 1 — God prepares the heart

Only God's renewing grace prepares the heart for every good work. By ourselves, we lack even the ability to think or speak what is truly wise and good.

Verse 2 — Our self-judgment is biased

Ignorance, pride and self-flattery make us partial judges of our own conduct.

Verse 3 — Entrust your cares to God

Lay the burden of your concerns upon God, leaving it there in faith and dependence on him.

Verse 4 — God overrules the wicked

God uses the wicked to execute righteous vengeance upon one another, and he will be glorified by their destruction at last.

Verse 5 — Pride cannot escape judgment

Even when sinners join forces to strengthen themselves, they cannot escape God's judgment.

Verse 6 — Mercy and truth in Christ

Through God's mercy and truth revealed in Jesus Christ, believers' sins are removed and sin's power is broken.

Verse 7 — God can reconcile enemies

The One who holds every human heart in his hand can move even someone's enemies to make peace.

Verse 8 — Honest means are better

A small possession honestly acquired is more useful and blessed than a large fortune obtained by wrongdoing.

Verse 9 — The Lord directs our steps

If we make God's glory our goal and his will our rule, he will guide our steps by his Spirit and grace.

Kings and judges on earth must be just and govern in the fear of God.

Verse 11 — Justice in commerce

Honesty and justice in dealings between people are appointed by God.

Verse 12 — A ruler's true security

A ruler who exercises authority rightly finds justice to be the surest protection of that office.

Verse 13 — Wise speech in positions of trust

Those appointed to authority should know how to speak what is appropriate and useful.

Verses 14 and 15 — Value God's favor above royal favor

How foolish it is to seek the favor of an earthly ruler by forfeiting the favor of God.

Verse 16 — The worth of wisdom

Only true wisdom provides deep joy and lasting satisfaction of spirit.

Verse 17 — Keep far from evil

A sincerely godly person avoids even the appearance of wrongdoing. Blessed are those who walk in Christ and follow his Spirit.

Verse 18 — Pride precedes judgment

When people defy God's judgments and think themselves beyond their reach, punishment may be close. Rather than fearing other people's pride, fear pride within your own heart.

Verse 19 — Humility before God

Humility may be despised by the world, but it is infinitely better than pride that turns God into an enemy. Those who understand his word will find what is good.

Verse 21 — True wisdom lives within

Someone whose wisdom has taken root in the heart is more genuinely prudent than people who possess dazzling natural talents alone.

Verse 22 — Wisdom refreshes others

A wise person is to friends and neighbors like water upon thirsty ground.

Verse 23 — Know yourself to speak well

A wise person's understanding of the heart helps that person discover what should be said to others.

Verse 24 — God's word heals

The word of God is a remedy for the diseases that weaken the soul.

Verse 25 — Do not deceive your soul

The warning calls everyone to take care against self-deception regarding spiritual condition and salvation.

Verse 26 — Work for eternal food

We must seek the food that endures to everlasting life rather than laboring only for what perishes.

Verses 27 and 28 — The labor of doing wrong

Ungodly people often work harder to cause harm than would be needed to do good. Those who spread malicious whispers separate close friends—an especially hateful yet common evil.

Verses 29 and 30 — Violence blinds its servants

Some people work as much harm as they can through force and violence, while refusing to recognize where their actions lead.

Verse 31 — Let old age be honorable

Older people especially should be found walking in the way of faith and obedience.

Verse 32 — Self-control exceeds military strength

Governing our own passions requires steadier and more demanding discipline than winning a victory over a human enemy.

Verse 33 — Submit to Providence

Whatever God appoints in the matters we have entrusted to him, we should receive as his wise determination. Blessed are those who submit to his will, knowing he understands what is truly good for them.

Verse 1 — Peace at home

Love and peace within a household are essential to the comfort and happiness of human life.

Verse 2 — Wisdom is greater than birth

A wise servant can be more deserving of honor and family affection than a son who lives in wickedness.

Verse 3 — Trials expose the heart

God tests our hearts through suffering, often revealing sins that still remain even within a believer.

Verse 4 — The danger of flattery

People living in sin often welcome flatterers, especially false teachers who reinforce them in wrongdoing.

Verse 5 — Do not mock the poor

Mocking poverty shows contempt for God's providence and his commands.

Verse 6 — The value of faithful parents

It is an honor and blessing for grown children to continue enjoying the presence and guidance of wise, godly parents.

Verse 7 — Good speech needs a good life

In Proverbs, a fool means a wicked person. Excellent words do not fit such a person, because conduct contradicts speech.

Verse 8 — How gifts rule covetous hearts

People who make money their chief desire may do almost anything to acquire it. How much more should the gifts of God influence our hearts toward him!

Verse 9 — Forgive and overlook offenses

Peace is preserved by giving the most charitable interpretation possible and not continually recalling every wrong spoken or done against us.

Verse 10 — The wise receive correction

A gentle rebuke enters not only the thoughts but the heart of someone who is wise.

Verse 11 — Rebellion invites judgment

Satan and his messengers are allowed to confront those who persist stubbornly in evil.

Verse 12 — Avoid uncontrolled rage

Guard your own passions carefully, and avoid the company of people whose anger is violent and unrestrained.

Verse 13 — Do not repay good with evil

Returning evil for good is devilish conduct and can bring a curse upon one's household.

Verse 14 — Stop conflict before it begins

The earliest stage of a quarrel is especially dangerous. Resist it at the first sign; if possible, leave the dispute before it even begins.

Verse 15 — Judge impartially

God is offended both when a guilty person is declared innocent and when someone innocent is condemned.

Verse 16 — Do not neglect true wisdom

It is absurd for human beings to disregard God's favor and their own true interests.

Verse 17 — Faithful friendship and Christ

Changes in wealth or circumstances should not weaken love for friends and relatives. Yet only Christ deserves unreserved confidence. In him this promise of faithful friendship finds its greatest fulfillment.

Verse 18 — Human guarantees and the divine Surety

Never endanger your family by rash financial promises. But Christ's decision to become Surety for humanity was a glorious act of divine wisdom: he was fully able to pay the debt.

Verse 19 — Avoid anger and vain display

Those seeking a peaceful conscience should avoid needless provocations to anger. Living above one's means in order to impress others is a road toward ruin.

Verse 20 — Schemes and uncontrolled speech

Evil plans bring no real advantage. Many people have suffered severely because they could not restrain their tongues.

Verse 21 — Sorrow from a foolish child

The wickedness and folly of a child cause profound grief to even wise and godly parents.

Verse 22 — The mercy of cheerfulness

It is God's kindness that he permits us to rejoice, gives reasons for joy, and through his grace can make our hearts capable of enjoying it.

Verse 23 — Bribes reveal guilt

The wicked can be willing to surrender even money they dearly love in order to escape the consequences of their crimes.

Verse 24 — Keep wisdom in view

Prudent people continually keep God's word before them. Foolish people cannot settle their thoughts or persevere steadily in a good purpose.

Verse 25 — Children can wound both parents

Wicked children despise a father's rightful authority and a mother's tenderness.

Verse 26 — Do not punish duty

It is seriously wrong to blame or penalize someone for doing what duty requires.

Verses 27 and 28 — Temperance in speech

Wise people show themselves through calmness of spirit and control over the tongue. When they speak, they choose words that serve a purpose. God alone sees every heart perfectly and cannot be misled by appearances.

Verse 1 — Seek every means of spiritual growth

Those who want knowledge and grace should make use of every appropriate way of growing in them.

Verse 2 — Knowledge is not for display

People who study or profess religion only to have something impressive to show others have missed its true purpose.

Verse 3 — Shame follows sin

As soon as sin entered the world, shame followed it.

Verse 4 — The spring of wisdom

Wisdom stored in a believer's heart becomes a continual spring of wise words.

Verse 5 — Judge the cause, not the person

What matters is the justice of a case, not the social standing or identity of the person involved.

Verses 6 and 7 — The harm of uncontrolled speech

Wicked people cause extraordinary harm to themselves through words they refuse to govern.

Verse 8 — Do not sow suspicion

Spreading quarrels and whispers is contemptible. Even small beginnings of jealousy may produce dreadful consequences.

Verse 9 — Neglecting duty is also dangerous

Failure to perform known duties, including performing duties carelessly, may harm the soul just as surely as committing active sins.

Verses 10 and 11 — God's strong tower versus wealth's illusion

The Lord's divine power, revealed through Jesus Christ, is a strong tower for those who trust him. Wealthy people who put ultimate confidence in earthly possessions imagine they live behind high and secure walls. Those defenses will fail when most needed, leaving them before the judgment of the One they rejected as Savior.

Verse 12 — Pride and humility

Pride raises the heart before a fall. Genuine honor follows humility.

Verse 13 — Listen before answering

Eagerness mixed with self-confidence exposes a person to shame when answering before understanding.

Verse 14 — When the spirit is wounded

Firmness of character can sustain people through many bodily pains. But a conscience tortured by remorse overwhelms even human courage. What, then, will hell be like?

Verse 15 — Knowledge must reach the heart

We should seek knowledge not merely to fill the mind but to change the heart.

Verse 16 — Welcome at the throne of grace

Bless the Lord, who welcomes us to his throne without money and without price. May the gifts he bestows make room for him within our souls.

Verse 17 — Hear what opponents say

Listening to criticism from our enemies can help us form a fairer judgment of ourselves.

Verse 18 — The seriousness of drawing lots

Matters were sometimes entrusted to God by casting lots with solemn prayer. But the lot has been profaned when used for entertainment or to seek another person's possessions; Henry raises this as an objection to such practices now.

Verse 19 — Avoid quarrels among relatives

Great care is needed to prevent conflict between relatives and others bound together by obligation. Wisdom and grace make forgiveness easier; sinful corruption makes it harder.

Verse 20 — What fills the heart determines satisfaction

The word belly here stands for the heart. Our inward peace and contentment depend upon what fills that heart.

Verse 21 — A tongue can destroy lives

Many people have caused their own death or the death of others through malicious or dishonest speech.

Verse 22 — A good marriage is God's gift

A good wife is a great blessing to her husband and a sign of the Lord's favor.

Verse 23 — Poverty and humble petitions

Poverty teaches that we cannot simply order others to serve our wishes. Before the throne of God's grace we all come as needy petitioners.

Verse 24 — Christ, the faithful Friend

Jesus Christ never abandons those who love and trust him. For his sake, may we show that kind of friendship to others. Having loved his own in the world, he loved them to the end; we are his friends if we obey his commands (John 15:14).

Verse 1 — The honor of poor believers

A poor person who fears God is more honorable and happier than someone lacking wisdom and grace, however rich or powerful.

Verse 2 — Think before moving

A soul without knowledge cannot live wisely. Rushing ahead without considering where our feet are going is sinful.

Verse 3 — Folly followed by resentment

People get themselves into trouble through foolishness, then become angry about God's providential arrangements.

Verse 4 — The power money holds

This verse exposes how strongly money can attract and govern human affection.

Verse 5 — Small lies grow

People who habitually lie in ordinary conversation are moving toward the still graver sin of false testimony.

Verse 6 — All gifts come from God

We have no excuse for withholding wholehearted love from God. His gifts are innumerable, and even other people's kindnesses are fruits of his generosity.

Verse 7 — Christ understands abandonment

Even Christ was deserted by his disciples, but the Father remained with him. The Savior's experience of poverty and rejection encourages our faith.

Verse 8 — Love your soul rightly

Only those who acquire true wisdom love their own souls as they ought.

Verse 9 — The danger of lying

Lying is a destructive sin that brings condemnation.

Verse 10 — True enjoyment requires grace

Without wisdom and grace, a person has no rightful claim to lasting joy. Those enslaved to sin should not oppress people whom God has made free.

Verse 11 — Overcome evil with good

The greatest honor belongs to those who most consistently seek to overcome evil through good.

Verse 12 — Christ the King

Christ's wrath against his enemies is terrifying like a roaring lion, while his favor toward his people is refreshing like dew.

Verse 13 — The uncertainties of comfort

The world's vanity appears when our greatest griefs arise from relationships or possessions in which we expected the greatest comfort.

Verse 14 — A virtuous spouse is precious

A prudent and godly wife is worth more than houses and wealth.

Verse 15 — Sloth brings want

A lazy disposition produces poverty and need. The warning applies to spiritual life as well as earthly affairs.

Verse 16 — Grace does not cancel obedience

Keeping God's word protects us from what is truly harmful. We abuse the doctrine of free grace if we claim it makes obedience unnecessary. Those who live carelessly will die; the warning should awaken even hardened sinners.

Verse 17 — God values care for the poor

God has chosen people who are poor in this world to be rich in faith and heirs of his kingdom.

Verse 18 — Correct children with wise affection

Parents must overcome misguided softness and correct their children; this is one way to help children grow into people who bring comfort and are happy themselves.

Verse 19 — Indulgence feeds violent anger

A child allowed every desire without correction is likely to become an adult with an uncontrolled temper.

Verse 20 — Learn while young

Those hoping to be wise at life's end must receive teaching and proper guidance while they are young.

Verse 21 — Let our plans agree with God's will

What better thing can we desire than that all our plans should agree with God's holy purposes?

Verse 22 — Good intentions without ability

It is better to have the heart to do good but lack the means, than to have ample means but no desire to help.

Verse 23 — Reverence brings true satisfaction

Those who live in the fear of God gain lasting security, contentment and happiness.

Verse 24 — Laziness can become helplessness

Habitual idleness grows until a person no longer has energy even for necessary self-care.

Verse 25 — Gentle correction is effective

A mild rebuke often does more to reach someone with understanding than harsh punishment.

Verse 26 — Honor parents and protect them

A young person who wastes a father's possessions or leaves an aged mother destitute behaves shamefully and will be disgraced.

Verse 27 — Avoid corrupting speech

Young people wisely refuse to listen to conversation that would implant sinful principles in the mind.

Verse 28 — Delighting in sin

The worst sinners actively welcome opportunities to do wrong.

Verse 29 — Christ's suffering guarantees judgment's reality

Human unbelief cannot cancel God's warnings. When Christ bore sins that were not his own, he was not spared: divine justice fell upon our blessed Surety. How could stubborn sinners expect impunity?

Verse 1 — The folly of drunkenness

Even highly capable people, as well as those lacking education, may make themselves foolish through the taste and excitement of strong drink.

Verse 2 — Fear the greater King

Earthly rulers may terrify those who provoke them. How much more foolish it is to provoke the King of kings!

Verse 3 — Choose peace over quarrels

Seeking disputes is great folly. For peace's sake, be willing to yield even a claim that is technically just.

Verse 4 — Work now for a future harvest

Those who labor patiently in preparing for eternity are also likely to be diligent in honest earthly responsibilities.

Verse 5 — Draw out wise counsel

People capable of giving valuable advice do not always volunteer it. Those who patiently draw it out will be well rewarded.

Verse 6 — Do good rather than boast

It is rare to find people who do more good than they talk about, or than they even care to hear praised.

Verse 7 — Integrity gives peace to the family

Honest people need not constantly devise schemes or fear their past deceit. Their households also benefit from their integrity.

Verse 8 — The responsibility of good rulers

People in high authority who are themselves good can accomplish much good and prevent much evil.

Verse 9 — Cleansing is the Holy Spirit's work

By grace, some can truthfully say they are purer than before. But this improvement is the work of the Holy Spirit.

Verse 10 — God rejects dishonest commerce

Love of money produces many kinds of deceit. The Lord will not bless wealth acquired through fraudulent practices.

Verse 11 — Watch children's behavior

Parents should carefully observe their children's conduct so they can guide and correct them appropriately.

Verse 12 — Use God's gifts for God

All our powers, senses and abilities come from God and should be used for his service.

Verse 13 — Work rather than indulge idleness

Those who surrender themselves to sleep and pleasure may lack even life's necessities, which honest labor could have supplied.

Verse 14 — Do not cheat in bargaining

People sometimes manipulate sellers or buyers in order to get a favorable price. They should be ashamed of fraud and lies, not proud of a bargain.

Verse 15 — Knowledge exceeds riches

Those who prefer true knowledge to wealth follow the path of godliness and happiness. If we believed this fully, God's word would be cherished and worldly wealth would lose its seductive attraction.

Verse 16 — Avoid reckless guarantees

Those who guarantee obligations recklessly or entangle themselves in immoral relationships put themselves in danger. Such arrangements do not deserve our confidence.

Verse 17 — Fraud's sweetness turns bitter

Dishonest gain may taste sweet to a sinful mind pleased by its own cleverness, but the memory of it will become bitter.

Verse 18 — Counsel for spiritual conflict

We especially need wise counsel in spiritual warfare. God's word and Spirit are the best advisers on every question.

Verse 19 — Do not purchase flattering praise

People who trust someone simply because that person speaks pleasantly may pay dearly for such admiration.

Verse 20 — The misery of disrespecting parents

Children who persist in dishonoring their parents will find neither genuine peace nor comfort.

Verse 21 — Sudden riches can vanish

A fortune gained too quickly may disappear just as quickly.

Verse 22 — Wait for the Lord

Trust the Lord's timing, obey his will, and rely upon him for protection rather than seeking revenge.

Verse 23 — Dishonesty makes a bad bargain

A deal achieved through fraud eventually proves to be a loss.

Verse 24 — Depend on God for every undertaking

We cannot wisely plan our lives or manage our affairs independently of the Lord.

Verse 25 — Watch conscience's evasions

The excuses people offer to quiet their own consciences show how deceitful the fallen heart can be.

Verse 26 — Justice distinguishes right from wrong

Just authority should restrain and punish evil, distinguishing wicked conduct from virtuous conduct.

Verse 27 — Conscience as a lamp

The rational soul and conscience are like a lamp within us. We should use that light to examine our motives and attitudes by God's revealed will.

Verse 28 — The glories of God's throne

Mercy and truth are the glories of God's kingship.

Verse 29 — Different ages, different strengths

Both young and old possess distinctive advantages. Neither should envy or despise the other.

Verse 30 — Correction may purify

Severe correction can sometimes accomplish real good. Fallen human nature makes us dislike rebuke, but if God uses painful trials to purify our hearts and prepare us for his work, we have reason to thank him.
